original_question: Suppose I and J are finite sets and {N_i}_{i in I}, {M_j}_{j in J} are separable II1 factors such that the free products *_i in I NU_i and *_j in J MU_j are isomorphic. Determine whether I and J must be bijective and, up to permutation, the corresponding factors must be mutually elementarily equivalent.
target_in_paper: Problem 50 in the "Miscellaneous" section, i.e. the finite-family free-product rigidity question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right mathematical core: finite index sets, families of separable II1 factors, an isomorphism between the corresponding free products, and the intended conclusion that after reindexing by a permutation, corresponding free-product components should be only elementarily equivalent (not necessarily isomorphic). That is exactly the content of Problem 50. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The hypothesis should display the actual factor families (N_i)_{i∈I} and (M_j)_{j∈J}; the draft has typographical slips in the free-product notation ("NU_i" and "MU_j"). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

For a stand-alone formulation, it is best to say explicitly that these are the usual tracial free products of II1 factors, taken with respect to their canonical traces; the paper leaves that standard convention implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Replace the phrase "I and J must be bijective" with the precise conclusion that there exists a bijection σ:I→J, equivalently |I|=|J|. Problem 50 phrases the conclusion as holding "up to permutation." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
Spell out "up to permutation" as: there is a bijection σ:I→J such that N_i ≡ M_{σ(i)} for every i∈I. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Define "elementarily equivalent" in the paper’s sense for II1 factors: there exist ultrafilters U and V such that N^U ≅ M^V. This definition is given in the opening notation of the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
State explicitly that the isomorphism is an isomorphism of II1 factors (equivalently, of tracial von Neumann algebras). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Make clear that no extra assumptions are present: Problem 50 is asked for arbitrary separable II1 factors indexed by finite sets, with no added amenability, primeness, non-Gamma, or distinctness hypotheses. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
refined_question: Let I and J be finite sets, and let (N_i)_{i∈I} and (M_j)_{j∈J} be separable II1 factors. Suppose that their tracial free products are isomorphic as II1 factors: ∗_{i∈I} N_i ≅ ∗_{j∈J} M_j. Must there exist a bijection σ:I→J such that N_i ≡ M_{σ(i)} for every i∈I, where ≡ denotes elementary equivalence of II1 factors in the sense fixed at the start of the paper (equivalently, existence of ultrafilters U and V with N_i^U ≅ M_{σ(i)}^V)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact finite-family question stated as Problem 50. The nearby Problem 49 is the one-factor analogue, which confirms that Problem 50 is the intended multi-factor extension. The only real repairs needed are precision repairs: restore the correct free-product notation, formalize "up to permutation" via a bijection σ:I→J, and import the paper’s opening definition of elementary equivalence for II1 factors. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
